project.summary: Inventory bookkeeping for a small workshop: a SKU catalog and kit assembly.

A Catalog is used from one thread at a time.

project.name: recordsync
project.title: recordsync
project.summary: A small client for the record service. It maps HTTP-style status codes to exceptions and retries outages with exponential backoff.

contract: RecordClient.fetch(record_id) accepts ids that are non-empty strings of ASCII letters, digits and '-'; any other id raises ValueError without calling the transport. For status 200 the transport returns a JSON object and fetch returns its "data" member. Status 404 raises RecordMissing and status 401 or 403 raises AccessDenied; each makes exactly one transport call. Statuses 429, 502, 503 and 504, an OSError from the transport, and a 200 object without "data" count as outages: fetch makes at most `attempts` transport calls in total and then raises TransientError. Every other status raises FetchError, also with a single call.

contract: History.recent(count) returns a new array holding the newest min(count, size) entries, oldest first: recent(0) returns an empty array and a count larger than size returns every entry. count must be an integer of 0 or more; any other value throws RangeError. project.summary: Locates release artifacts across a set of download mirrors for a long-running package proxy.

contract: Locate probes every mirror concurrently and returns the URL of the first probe that succeeds; the context handed to the remaining probes is then cancelled. If every probe fails, the error matches ErrNotFound and wraps each probe error. If ctx ends first, Locate returns ctx.Err(). The artifact name must pass ValidateArtifact and mirrors must be non-empty; otherwise Locate returns an error without probing. Probes honour cancellation. The package proxy calls Locate for every request for the lifetime of the process.

project.name: profiles
project.title: profiles
project.summary: A thread-safe cache of configuration profiles loaded on first use from a pluggable backing store.

contract: Registry is shared between threads. get(name) returns the cached profile when there is one. Otherwise it loads the settings from the source, caches the new profile and returns it; a name the source does not know returns None and caches nothing. Two threads that miss at the same time may both call load, but the first insert wins and both receive the same Arc. Any name is accepted, including the empty string.

lines: //! Shared configuration profiles for worker threads.
/// A named list of settings, shared between threads through `Arc`.
/// Backing store for profiles, for example a directory of files.
/// `load` may block on I/O. It returns `None` when the store has no profile

check.summary: A worker thread calls get on an empty registry for a known name, again for the same name, and for an unknown name; the main thread waits three seconds for the results, then four threads request one more name concurrently.
check.failure_signature: CHECK-FAIL: get did not return within 3 s on a cache miss

lines: Err(_) => fail("get did not return within 3 s on a cache miss"),
fail("second get did not return the cached profile");
fail("absent profile cached or loads miscounted");

label.trigger: Any call for a name that is not cached yet. The MutexGuard created in the match scrutinee lives until the end of the whole match, so the None arm calls lock() on a mutex its own thread still holds.
label.expected_impact: The first lookup of every profile blocks its thread for good (std's Mutex is not reentrant). Every other thread that touches the registry then waits on the same lock, so the worker pool stalls on startup.

known_counterevidence.note: Binding the cloned Arc in its own statement ends the temporary guard at the semicolon, so the second lock() in the miss path is uncontended and load runs without the lock.
The entry().or_insert() insert is the correct way to honour the first-insert-wins rule; it is not the problem.

label.reviewer_notes: Cached hits work, so only the miss path shows it. The borrow checker accepts the code. A report that only says the lock is held while load runs is the same root cause and should count, provided it reaches the re-lock in the None arm.
